question.problem: If $u=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 4 \\ -5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ k \\ 5 \\ 6\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal vectors, then $k=$
question.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that their dot product is equal to zero.
First, let's calculate the dot product in terms of $k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =(-5)\cdot 1+4\cdot k+(-5)\cdot 5+(-3)\cdot 6 \\  & =-5+4k-25-18 \\  & =4k-48\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the dot product to zero, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4k-48 & =0 \\ 4k & =48 \\ k & =12.\end{aligned}
$$
